claims.text: Press TV aired Minister of Energy Reza Ghalami saying Iran's oil was still flowing despite 550 strikes on the Kharg tanker, on September 7
claims.note: Press TV (7 Sept) quoted Petroleum Minister Mohsen Paknejad: crude exports were not interrupted during the 40-day war despite more than 550 attacks on Kharg Island (the island, not a tanker). Name and title wrong.

claims.text: Iran proclaimed a 'restricted zone' just outside Hormuz, marked on civilian charts as a no-fly corridor
claims.note: An 8 Sept report mentions Iranian plans for a restricted zone in the strait; the no-fly corridor and charts detail is unsupported.

claims.note: Korea Times: foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said a military presence in the Gulf 'would amount to direct support for the aggressor'; an unnamed senior official told Al Mayadeen a Korean role would be 'direct military participation in the aggression'. Ali Shahriari not found.

edits.headline: Iran says it fired missiles at US carrier and destroyer near Hormuz
edits.subheadline: US Central Command said both warships evaded the attack and no American personnel were harmed, Anadolu Agency reported.
editorialBody: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a destroyer near the Strait of Hormuz early on September 6, and said both ships were damaged. US Central Command said both warships evaded the attack and no American personnel were harmed, Anadolu Agency reported.
Iran's petroleum minister, Mohsen Paknejad, said crude exports were not interrupted during the 40-day war despite more than 550 attacks on Kharg Island, Press TV reported.
Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baqaei, warned South Korea that a military presence in the Gulf would amount to direct support for the aggressor, the Korea Times reported.

Nepal held a national day of mourning on September 7 for more than 1,300 people killed in floods in Nepal and Tibet, the Associated Press reported. About 5,000 people were still missing, according to Nepal's disaster management agency.
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv after talks with President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, the Associated Press reported.
The SEC's rewrite of its crypto custody rules has entered White House review, The Defiant reported.
Huawei unveiled a trifold smartphone powered by a Kirin chip based on its Tau scaling law, the South China Morning Post reported.
